changes.before: Build the draft form with its labeled title and Save button. Put the Preview button outside it, associate it using form=draft, and give it the stated GET preview overrides.
changes.after: Give two submit buttons different jobs.

before: A form may have several submit buttons with different intentions. The particular button that initiates submission is the submitter. Its own name/value can join the form data; other submit buttons are not all included merely because they exist.

type="submit" chooses a submission button. name="intent" and value="save" or "preview" describe its contributed pair. form="draft" associates the outside Preview button with the form whose id is draft. formaction and formmethod on that submit button override the form’s action and method for that submission only. They do not rewrite the form element.

```html
<form id="draft" action="/save" method="post">
  <label for="title">Draft title</label><input id="title" name="title" value="Pond notes">
  <button id="save" type="submit" name="intent" value="save">Save draft</button>
</form>
<button id="preview" type="submit" form="draft" name="intent" value="preview" formaction="/preview" formmethod="get">Preview draft</button>
```
Activating Save requests POST /save with title and intent=save. Activating Preview requests GET /preview with title and intent=preview. GET exposes data in the URL query, so use only the fictional nonsensitive title here. The endpoints are not implemented. Constructing FormData(form) without a submitter does not simulate clicking a particular button; the exercise checks association and attributes without navigation.

Build the draft form with its labeled title and Save button. Put the Preview button outside it, associate it using form=draft, and give it the stated GET preview overrides. The supplied checks inspect markup or local form-data relationships; they do not submit a network request or certify a screen-reader or native-browser experience. Optional local practice: try the changed case in a disposable local page and explain the difference.
after: A form can have more than one submit button. The button someone uses is called the submitter. Its own name and value can tell the receiving service which action was chosen.

A submit button can sit outside a form. Give it `form="draft"` to connect it to the form with `id="draft"`. Its `formaction` and `formmethod` can choose a different destination and method for that button only.

This form offers Save draft and Preview draft.

```html
<form id="draft" action="/save" method="post">
  <label for="title">Draft title</label><input id="title" name="title" value="Pond notes">
  <button id="save" type="submit" name="intent" value="save">Save draft</button>
</form>
<button id="preview" type="submit" form="draft" name="intent" value="preview" formaction="/preview" formmethod="get">Preview draft</button>
```

Save uses the form’s POST request to `/save` and adds `intent=save`. Preview uses GET to `/preview` and adds `intent=preview`. The other button’s value is left out. The form’s own settings stay the same.

Build the shown form with its labeled title and Save button. Put Preview after `</form>`, then connect it with `form="draft"`. Add its preview settings and run the checks. The practice checks these connections without sending anything; it does not include working save or preview services.

before.question: Remove only form="draft" from the outside Preview button. Does its name/value still associate it with that form?
choices: Yes, formaction automatically finds the nearest form anywhere in the page.
No. Being outside, it now has no form owner; its name is not a form link.
Yes, matching intent names connect all buttons to one form.
before.explanation: The form attribute references a form ID. name contributes data only when a button is an associated submitter; it does not establish ownership.

after.question: You remove form="draft" from Preview, which is outside the form. Is it still connected to that form?
choices: No. Its name and value do not connect it.
Yes, the shared name intent connects it.
after.explanation: An outside button needs the form attribute to identify its form. Its name describes sent data, not that connection.
